full_statement: Let $v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb R^m$ be vectors with Euclidean norms $\|v_j\|_2\le 1$. Equivalently, let $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ be a real matrix whose columns have $\ell_2$ norm at most $1$. A signing $x\in\{-1,+1\}^n$ has discrepancy $\|Ax\|_\infty$, the largest absolute coordinate of the signed vector sum. The Komlos conjecture asks whether there is a universal constant $K$ such that every such matrix admits a signing with $\|Ax\|_\infty\le K$, independent of the number of rows $m$ and columns $n$. The conjecture implies Beck-Fiala after scaling each degree-$t$ incidence column by $1/\sqrt t$: a constant Komlos bound would give $O(\sqrt t)$ discrepancy for degree-$t$ set systems. The historically open problem is the full dimension-free constant bound for arbitrary real unit-column matrices, with no distributional, smoothed-input, bounded-rank, or sparsity assumption. An algorithmic solution would additionally find the signing in polynomial time. Status at 2026-11-09: Guo, Fang, and Lu's September 2026 preprint claims the full Komlos conjecture (Theorem 1.1); Karingula and Lovett give a subsequent elementary-proof preprint. This record flags a claimed resolution, pending verification.
background: Historical context before the 2026 full-resolution claims: The Komlos conjecture is a central vector-balancing problem. Given vectors of Euclidean norm at most one, choose signs so that every coordinate of the signed sum is bounded by a universal constant. It generalizes Beck-Fiala because the incidence columns of a degree-$t$ set system can be scaled to unit length, and a constant Komlos bound would imply $O(\sqrt t)$ Beck-Fiala discrepancy. The conjecture is also a benchmark for algorithmic discrepancy, convex geometry, and rounding. Banaszczyk's theorem gives the best classical asymptotic bound $O(\sqrt{\log n})$, and recent work of Bansal and Jiang improves this to roughly $\widetilde O(\log^{1/4} n)$, but the desired dimension-free constant was not settled by those earlier results. Status at 2026-11-09: Guo, Fang, and Lu's September 2026 preprint claims the full Komlos conjecture (Theorem 1.1); Karingula and Lovett give a subsequent elementary-proof preprint.
open_problem: Verify the claimed resolution of the original conjecture. Historical target: Prove or refute the Komlos conjecture: unit Euclidean norm vectors can be signed to have $O(1)$ discrepancy in every coordinate.
known_results:
Historical context before the 2026 full-resolution claims: Banaszczyk proved that unit-column matrices admit discrepancy $O(\sqrt{\log n})$, and Bansal, Dadush, and Garg gave an efficient algorithm matching that bound. The conjectured answer is $O(1)$. Bansal, Jiang, Meka, Singla, and Sinha proved Komlos in a smoothed-analysis setting when the input vectors are perturbed and sufficiently numerous relative to the dimension. Bansal and Jiang recently improved the pre-September-2026 worst-case general dependence to $\widetilde O(\log^{1/4}n)$ using affine spectral-independence constraints in an SDP-guided random walk. They also obtain improved Beck-Fiala consequences. Lower bounds show that the optimal universal constant, if the conjecture holds, cannot be too small, but no superconstant lower bound is known. The pre-September-2026 gap was between constant and about a fourth-root logarithm. Status at 2026-11-09: Guo, Fang, and Lu's September 2026 preprint claims the full Komlos conjecture (Theorem 1.1); Karingula and Lovett give a subsequent elementary-proof preprint.

Algorithmic follow-up: Guo, Fang, and Lu, arXiv:2609.23540v2, Theorem 1.1, report a deterministic polynomial-time real-RAM algorithm with discrepancy at most $8272$. Xiaoyu Li, arXiv:2609.30044v1, Theorem 1.1, reduces this to below $99$ and proves polynomial bit complexity for rational inputs. Emile Anand and Peter Chen, arXiv:2610.20995v1, Theorem 1.1, report the same discrepancy in $\widetilde O(L_{\mathrm{in}}+n^\omega)$ expected bit operations. Thus algorithmic constant discrepancy is also addressed by current preprints, not left wholly unresolved. These statements were checked, not their full proofs.

agent_guidance.suitable_approaches: Check the cited full-resolution and algorithmic theorems, including precision and computational-model assumptions. Treat any new target about sharp constants as a separate question.
agent_guidance.verification_notes: A claimed proof must handle arbitrary real matrices with column Euclidean norms at most one and must produce a numerical bound independent of $m,n$, rank, sparsity, and coefficient precision. The proof should output or certify a full signing of all columns; partial-coloring arguments must include an iteration analysis showing that no logarithmic factor is accumulated. A verifier should reject arguments that only prove Beck-Fiala, random or smoothed input cases, bounded-rank or bounded-row-norm cases, vector systems in special position, or $\widetilde O(\log^{1/4}n)$-type bounds unless they are explicitly presented as partial progress. A counterexample would need a family of unit-column matrices with discrepancy tending to infinity, not just examples that defeat Banaszczyk-style algorithms. The relevant theorem statements and proof framework were read, but this audit is not an independent proof verification; no peer-reviewed publication was established.
